neighbours.label: ' feasible' / ' unbiased': technical adjectives saying a solution or estimator meets a formal admissibility criterion
fire: The simplex method moves from one feasible vertex to the next until no improvement remains.
If the constraints contradict each other, the linear program has no feasible point at all.
The heuristic quickly finds a feasible schedule, although it may not be the cheapest one.
The sample mean is an unbiased estimator of the population mean under random sampling.
Phase one of the algorithm searches for an initial feasible basis before optimising.
Under the Gauss-Markov conditions, least squares gives the best linear unbiased estimate.
Branch and bound discards any node whose relaxation has no feasible region left.
The solver reports the first feasible solution it finds and then keeps improving it.
quiet: The simplex method moves from one corner of the polytope to the next until no improvement remains.
If the constraints contradict each other, the linear program cannot be solved at all.
The heuristic quickly finds a schedule for the week, although it may not be the cheapest one.
The sample mean is a simple summary of the data under random sampling.
Phase one of the algorithm searches for an initial starting point before optimising.
Under the Gauss-Markov conditions, least squares gives a closed-form estimate.
Branch and bound discards any node whose bound is worse than the best value so far.
The solver reports the first solution it finds and then keeps improving it.
